text.p: Following are some of the major events which occurred on September 22 in history.
1515 - Anne of Cleves, fourth wife of King Henry VIII of England, born.
1735 - Sir Robert Walpole became the first British prime minister to occupy 10 Downing Street in London.
1776 - Nathan Hale, American patriot, was hanged in New York by the British for being a spy during the American Revolution.
1791 - Michael Faraday, English physicist and chemist, born. Noted for his experiments with electricity.
1792 - France was declared a republic.
1828 - Shaka, Zulu chieftain and founder of the Zulu empire, was killed by his two half-brothers after he became insane.
1862 - Otto von Bismarck became premier of Prussia.
1862 - U.S. President Abraham Lincoln declared all slaves in rebellious states would be free from January 1, 1863.
1880 - Dame Christabel Pankhurst, English suffragette, born. Prominent in the struggle for votes for women. Daughter of women's suffrage campaigner Emmeline Pankhurst.
1882 - Wilhelm Keitel, German World War Two field marshal, born.
1885 - Joseph Benedict Chifley, Australian statesman, born. Prime minister 1945-49, and leader of the Labor Party 1945-51.
1914 - German U-boat sank British cruisers Aboukir, Hogue and Cressy in the North Sea, killing more than 1,400.
1915 - Battle of Champagne began with one of the heaviest bombardments of World War One preceding the French attack.
1934 - The worst pit disaster in Britain for 21 years, an explosion and fire at the Gresford Mine in Wales, killed more than 260 miners.
1940 - French Indo-China signed agreement to allow Japan to station troops there. The Japanese, claiming not to have heard of the agreement, bombed Tongking.

1949 - British, Canadian and American governments jointly announced they had recently detected an atomic explosion in the Soviet Union. The blast, initially denied by Moscow, was later revealed to be the first test of an atomic weapon by the Soviet Union and occurred on August 29.
1955 - Commercial television began in Britain in opposition to the British Broadcasting Corporation. The first advertisement screened was for toothpaste.
1960 - Mali gained independence from France.
1965 - After a 17-day war over Kashmir, India and Pakistan agreed to a ceasefire.
1969 - China said it had conducted its first underground nuclear test.
1970 - Abdul Razak succeeded Abdul Rahman as prime minister of Malaysia.
1975 - An assassination attempt was made on U.S. President Gerald Ford in San Francisco by Sara Jane Moore. It was the second attempt in 17 days.
1980 - The Gulf War broke out when Iraq invaded Iran in an attempt to control the Shatt al-Arab waterway.
1985 - French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius admitted that French secret agents acting under orders sank the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior in New Zealand.
1989 - An Irish Republican Army bomb attack killed 10 at the Royal Marines School of Music in Deal, England.
1989 - Irving Berlin, U.S. songwriter, died aged 101.
1989 - Christian army chief General Michel Aoun accepted an Arab League plan to end the war in Lebanon.
1990 - Saudi Arabia expelled Yemeni and Jordanian diplomats and cut off oil supplies to Jordan because of their support for Iraq.
1993 - The Sunset Limited, an Amtrak train carrying about 200 people, plunged into a swamp near Mobile, Alabama after a bridge apparently collapsed, killing at least 47.
1995 - After nearly nine months of testimony, the defence and prosecution rested their cases at the O.J. Simpson murder trial in Los Angeles.
